> # VibeBuilder Implementation Plan
>
> ## Summary
> Build VibeBuilder as a SELISE Blocks Construct/Vite React app, because the repo is empty and Blocks deployment is documented around Construct-based projects. The app will include IAM authentication, isolated user workspaces, a drag-and-drop page editor, JSON layout persistence through Blocks Data Gateway, image persistence through Blocks Storage/Media, autosave, and a public live-site renderer.
>
> Use these references during implementation: [Blocks API Overview](https://docs.seliseblocks.com/reference/), [Data Gateway](https://docs.seliseblocks.com/cloud/others/data-gateway/), [Storage](https://docs.seliseblocks.com/cloud/Data/storage/), [Authentication](https://docs.seliseblocks.com/cloud/iam/authentication), and [Construct React](https://github.com/SELISEdigitalplatforms/blocks-construct-react).
>
> ## Key Changes
> - Scaffold the frontend with the SELISE Blocks CLI using the provided project configuration, then adapt the generated Construct React app instead of starting from a generic React template.
> - Install/use the requested frontend skills during execution:
>   - `frontend-design`
>   - `vercel-react-best-practices`
>   - `find-skills`
>   - Keep the already available React best-practices checklist as the final TSX review pass.
> - Configure environment variables for:
>   - Blocks API URL
>   - project slug
>   - app domain
>   - X-Blocks-Key, stored in env files and not hardcoded in source
> - Add app routes:
>   - `/login` and existing IAM auth flow
>   - `/app` workspace dashboard
>   - `/app/sites/:siteId/pages/:pageId` editor
>   - `/site/:siteSlug/:pageSlug` public renderer
> - Build a polished SaaS/productivity UI, not a marketing landing page: compact dashboard, editor shell, left component palette, center canvas, right properties inspector, top page/publish controls.
>
> ## Data And Interfaces
> Create Blocks Data Gateway schemas with owner-isolated access rules:
>
> - `Website`
>   - `id`, `ownerId`, `name`, `slug`, `status`, `createdAt`, `updatedAt`, `publishedAt`
> - `Page`
>   - `id`, `websiteId`, `ownerId`, `name`, `slug`, `sortOrder`, `draftLayout`, `publishedLayout`, `createdAt`, `updatedAt`
> - `Asset`
>   - `id`, `ownerId`, `websiteId`, `fileName`, `url`, `mimeType`, `size`, `createdAt`
>
> Use JSON layout objects like:
>
> ```ts
> type VibePageLayout = {
>   version: 1;
>   blocks: VibeBlock[];
> };
>
> type VibeBlock = {
>   id: string;
>   type: "hero" | "text" | "gallery" | "contact";
>   props: Record<string, unknown>;
> };
> ```
>
> Editor behavior:
> - Drag components from the palette into the canvas.
> - Reorder existing blocks using stable IDs.
> - Edit text, colors, images, alignment, and spacing in the inspector.
> - Autosave draft JSON with debounce.
> - Publish copies `draftLayout` to `publishedLayout`.
>
> Media behavior:
> - Upload files through Blocks Storage/Media.
> - Store returned URLs in `Asset`.
> - Reference uploaded image URLs inside block props.
>
> ## Implementation Steps
> - Bootstrap Construct:
>   - Install `@seliseblocks/cli` if needed.
>   - Run the Blocks web scaffold command into the repo or a temporary folder, then normalize it into the current repo.
>   - Use Node 20 if the generated app has issues with the current Node 25 runtime.
> - Add builder modules:
>   - `auth` integration wrapper around Construct/IAM session state.
>   - `blocksApi` client for Data Gateway GraphQL and storage calls.
>   - `builderStore` using Zustand for canvas state, selected block, dirty state, and autosave status.
>   - `componentRegistry` defining each Vibe Component’s defaults, editable props, renderer, and inspector controls.
> - Build UI:
>   - Workspace dashboard for creating/deleting websites and pages.
>   - Editor shell with dnd-kit for drag/drop and reorder.
>   - Inspector controls using existing Construct/Radix/shadcn-style primitives.
>   - Live renderer that only reads published layouts and supports multi-page navigation.
> - Portal/manual configuration:
>   - If Data Gateway schemas, RLS/CLS, storage folders, or deployment toggles cannot be configured from CLI/API, use the open Blocks Cloud UI in Arc/Computer Use to configure them.
> - Deployment:
>   - Keep `main` mapped to production.
>   - Build locally first, then push when ready so Blocks can deploy through the connected repo.
>
> ## Test Plan
> - Run `npm install`, `npm run lint`, `npm run build`, and available Vitest tests.
> - Verify auth flow reaches the dashboard after login.
> - Verify workspace isolation by ensuring created websites/pages are filtered by current user ID.
> - Verify editor flows:
>   - create website
>   - create pages
>   - add blocks
>   - reorder blocks
>   - edit props
>   - upload/select image
>   - autosave refresh recovery
>   - delete page
>   - publish
> - Verify public renderer:
>   - published pages load without editor chrome
>   - draft-only edits do not appear before publishing
>   - navigation between pages works by slug
> - Perform a browser visual pass for desktop and mobile to catch layout overlap, text clipping, blank canvas states, and broken image rendering.
>
> ## Assumptions
> - The project should prioritize a complete class-project MVP over deep CMS/admin features.
> - The public route will use `/site/:siteSlug/:pageSlug` on the Blocks app domain unless SELISE Blocks requires a different route shape.
> - User registration/login will rely on SELISE IAM/Construct auth, not a custom auth backend.
> - All durable data will go through SELISE Blocks services; no Firebase, local SQL, or custom database will be introduced.
> - Secrets and project keys stay in environment configuration, not source code.
</details>

What’s now in place:
- Node runtime pinned to `24` via `.nvmrc`.
- SELISE Construct scaffold normalized into this repo.
- Requested skills installed locally and ignored from git.
- Routes added:
  - `/login`

  - `/site/:siteSlug/:pageSlug`

- `.env.example` added with placeholders; real Blocks values are kept in ignored local env files.

- `npm run lint`

Picked up from where I left off and finished the last verification pass.

VibeBuilder is now implemented as a SELISE Blocks/Vite React app with the full MVP shape: authenticated workspace routes, website/page management, a polished drag-and-drop editor, expanded component palette, inspector customization, autosave/publish flow, image upload/URL controls, and a public renderer at `/site/:siteSlug/:pageSlug`.

I also configured Blocks Cloud Data Gateway in Chrome and published the schemas:

- `VibeWebsite`
- `VibePage`
- `VibeAsset`

The app persistence is aligned to those schemas using owner/query fields plus JSON layout payloads, rather than a local database. Local fallback remains only for dev resilience.

Validation completed under Node 24:

```bash
npx -p node@24 npm run lint
npx -p node@24 npm run build
npx -p node@24 npm test
```

All passed. Build only produced non-blocking dependency/chunk warnings. I also browser-verified the editor, mobile preview toggle, and public renderer. The dev server was stopped cleanly afterward.

To run it again:

```bash
npx -p node@24 npm run dev -- --host 127.0.0.1
```

Then open `http://127.0.0.1:3000/app`.

> Verified in Chrome: `/login` now visibly has Sign up, local demo credentials, and a working “Continue in demo workspace” path that lands on `/app`. I’m stopping the temporary server and then I’ll give you the short “how to log in” answer.
>
> <details><summary>Ran 4 commands</summary>
>
> - Ran `lsof -ti tcp:3001`
> - Ran `kill 32501 33909`
> - Ran `npx -p node@24 npm run dev -- --host 127.0.0.1`
> - Ran `lsof -ti tcp:3001`
>
> </details>
</details>

Fixed. The login page was hiding signup because Blocks IAM says signup is disabled, and the demo credential banner did not include `127.0.0.1`.

I updated [signin.tsx](./src/modules/auth/components/signin/signin.tsx) so `/login` now shows:

- A visible **Sign up** link.
- The SELISE demo credentials on `127.0.0.1`.
- A dev-only **Continue in demo workspace** button that logs you into a local demo account and sends you to `/app`.

For local work, use **Continue in demo workspace**. For real SELISE IAM, enable signup in Blocks IAM settings or use an existing IAM user.

Verified:

```bash
npx -p node@24 npm run lint
npx -p node@24 npm run build
```

Both pass. I also browser-tested `/login` and confirmed the demo button reaches `/app`.

One small thing: if your current app is still running on port `3000`, restart the dev server so it picks up this change.

> One wrinkle: because the browser is already signed into the demo session, the route middleware sends `/signup` back to `/app`. The actual blank signup issue is fixed in the page, but to see the signup form you’ll need to log out or clear the demo auth state. I’m checking the middleware now to see whether this redirect is expected and whether the user flow needs a clearer sign-out.
>
> <details><summary>Explored 3 files</summary>
>
> - Read `./src/state/client-middleware.tsx`
> - Read `./src/routes/auth.route.tsx`
> - Read `./src/layout/auth-layout/auth-layout.tsx`
>
> </details>
>
> I found why my browser jumped back to `/app`: `AuthLayout` redirects every authenticated auth-page visit to `/`. That makes `/signup` hard to inspect after using demo mode, so I’m narrowing that redirect to the login page only. Then `/signup` can show the form even while you’re already in a demo session.
>

> </details>

> I found the missing switch in Blocks Cloud: IAM → Access Manager → Signup Settings has `Allow signup` unchecked, even though the API settings endpoint reports the child methods. The next external action would be saving an IAM signup configuration in SELISE Cloud, which changes who can create accounts for this project. Please confirm: should I enable `Allow signup`, keep `Email and password` and `SSO` checked, and click `Save` in Blocks Cloud?
>
> While that confirmation is pending, I’m continuing the app QA locally. The IAM modal is parked open in Chrome; I’ll only save it after you confirm.

> # VibeBuilder Next Pass Plan
>
> ## Summary
> Continue from Cursor’s overhaul, preserving the SELISE Blocks integration and the new 39-component editor. The next pass should make VibeBuilder feel like a polished, publishable SaaS builder: dark-only, high-contrast, fast, visually distinctive, and capable of producing beautiful example sites end-to-end.
>
> ## Key Changes
> - **Design Polish**
>   - Establish one dark-only “Obsidian Studio” visual system: ink background `#080A0F`, elevated panels `#10131D`, teal/lime accent, warm coral highlights, readable off-white text.
>   - Remove remaining SELISE/Construct branding from visible app chrome and replace it with VibeBuilder brand language, favicon/manifest/OG polish.
>   - Audit all text/background pairs in workspace, editor, auth, inspector, public renderer, templates, buttons, inputs, menus, and empty states for contrast.
>   - Upgrade starter templates so published sites look genuinely impressive, not test-like: agency landing, creator portfolio, SaaS pricing, local business, event launch.
>
> - **Elementor-Inspired Builder Features**
>   - Add a **Navigator/Layers panel** showing all blocks, current selection, reorder controls, duplicate/delete, and quick jump.
>   - Add responsive per-device controls for key style fields: spacing, alignment, columns, font size, image position, visibility.
>   - Add global site style settings: colors, fonts, radius, button style, section width, background, favicon/SEO/home page.
>   - Add template actions: insert full-page template, insert section template, save current page as reusable template in local/Blocks data.
>   - Add stronger editor ergonomics: right-click/context menu, clearer hover/selected states, drop zones between blocks, command palette shortcuts, autosave status details.
>
> - **Data And SELISE Completion**
>   - Verify real SELISE IAM signup/login with a tempmail account through activation, within platform safety requirements.
>   - Configure or repair SELISE Data Gateway schemas so `VibeWebsites`, `VibePages`, and `VibeAssets` stop falling back to local demo cache.
>   - Keep local demo fallback only as development resilience, not as the primary success path.
>   - Confirm media upload uses SELISE Storage/Media and saved asset URLs persist through refresh and publish.
>   - Preserve owner isolation: logged-in users only list and edit their own websites/pages/assets.
>
> - **Performance**
>   - Memoize block renderers and inspector field rendering so typing in the inspector does not re-render the whole canvas unnecessarily.
>   - Split heavy builder-only code with lazy routes so public sites and auth pages do not load the full editor bundle.
>   - Debounce/throttle autosave and style updates separately: instant local UI, delayed network writes.
>   - Optimize DnD for large pages: stable block IDs, minimal JSON comparisons, avoid full-layout stringification in hot paths.
>   - Add lightweight render profiling during QA for pages with 40+ blocks.
>
> ## Test Plan
> - Run under Node 24:
>   - `npm run lint`
>   - `npm run build`
>   - `npm test -- --run`
> - Browser QA:
>   - Signup with tempmail, activate account, login, logout, login again.
>   - Create site from each template, create/rename/delete pages, add/reorder/duplicate/delete blocks.
>   - Test all 39 components: content edit, style edit, advanced edit, responsive preview, save, refresh persistence.
>   - Upload/select images, publish, open public site, verify editor chrome is absent.
>   - Confirm draft changes do not appear publicly until publish.
>   - Check desktop/tablet/mobile for clipping, overlap, unreadable contrast, broken images, and drag lag.
> - Performance QA:
>   - Build a 40+ block page and verify inspector typing, drag reorder, preview mode switching, and autosave remain responsive.
>
> ## Assumptions
> - Keep the app dark-only; no dark/light toggle.
> - Keep the current React/Vite/SELISE Blocks architecture and Cursor’s recent 39-component work.
> - Use Elementor only as feature inspiration, not as code to port.
> - Prioritize class-project completeness: real IAM, real Blocks persistence, strong builder UX, and beautiful published examples over broad CMS complexity.
</details>

Implemented the final polish pass and left the dev server running at:

`http://127.0.0.1:3000`

What changed:
- Added the new **Navigator/Layers** panel with select, move, duplicate, delete, and hide controls.
- Fixed block re-selection after clicking away; verified selecting from canvas/layers brings the inspector back.
- Added right-click block context actions: duplicate, move, copy style, paste style, reset style, open navigator, delete.
- Added responsive visibility controls to every block’s Advanced tab.
- Switched site defaults to the dark Obsidian-style theme and cleaned up remaining low-contrast/light inspector fields.
- Expanded templates to 6 polished starters: blank, SaaS landing, agency portfolio, pricing, restaurant/local, event launch.
- Improved dashboard template layout and thumbnails.
- Lazy-loaded VibeBuilder workspace/editor/public routes.
- Optimized autosave cache updates and removed whole-layout stringify from the hot block update path.
- Removed visible SELISE/Construct branding from the app-facing auth/media surfaces I found.

- `npx -p node@24 npm run lint` passed with warnings only.
- `npx -p node@24 npm run build` passed.
- `npx -p node@24 npm test -- --run` passed: 552 tests.

Not fully verified: real SELISE tempmail signup/activation and live Blocks Data Gateway schema creation. I verified the working local/demo flow end to end; the real cloud path still depends on the Blocks Cloud IAM/Data schemas being correctly enabled for the project.

> ## Summary
> Refine the Vibe builder without changing functionality: replace the current mark with a custom serif “V” identity, move builder controls into a compact left-tab workflow, make Layers a detached floating panel, remove glassmorphism/blur effects, improve contrast, and tighten React performance/bundle hygiene. Scope the “30% smaller” density change to builder chrome only, not published site content.
>
> ## Key Changes
> - **Brand and Icons**
>   - Replace `VibeMark` with a custom CSS/SVG serif “V” lettermark: dark enamel tile, off-white serif V, subtle flat border/accent, no gradient-glass treatment.
>   - Update `VibeWordmark` spacing/type so it feels editorial and premium while staying readable at collapsed/expanded sizes.
>   - Replace Vibe/editor chrome Lucide usage with already-installed `@radix-ui/react-icons`; do not add a new icon package.
>   - Remove Vibe-specific `lucide-react` imports from editor chrome, palette, inspector, layers, asset picker, command palette, workspace dashboard, public loader, logo close button, and main shell where practical.
>   - Keep non-Vibe legacy Construct modules untouched unless they are directly imported by the builder shell.
>
> - **Editor Layout and UX**
>   - Rework the editor into a compact left-side tabbed studio rail:
>     - `Insert`: component palette/search/quick insert.
>     - `Edit`: selected block inspector with existing Content/Style/Advanced groups inside.
>     - `Page`: page list, create page, rename current page, delete page.
>     - `Site`: site settings entry points and publish/live utilities.
>   - Remove the persistent right inspector column; selected block editing appears in the left `Edit` tab.
>   - Make Layers/Navigator a detached floating panel toggled from the toolbar/left rail, positioned over the canvas with solid panel styling, draggable only if existing primitives make this low-risk; otherwise fixed at top-left of canvas.
>   - Preserve all current actions: add, drag/drop, select/reselect, edit fields, upload/pick images, duplicate, delete, move, undo/redo, save, publish, page navigation, command palette, context menu, responsive preview, zoom.
>   - Apply builder-chrome density reduction: smaller panel widths, tighter padding, smaller toolbar buttons, smaller palette cards, smaller tabs, more compact inspector fields. Do not shrink public renderer block typography/spacing.
>
> - **Contrast and Visual Cleanup**
>   - Remove all visible `backdrop-blur`, `blur-*`, and “glass” UI treatments from builder/auth/workspace/editor surfaces touched by this pass.
>   - Replace glass styles with solid near-black/graphite surfaces plus opacity-only overlays where depth is useful.
>   - Rename/remove builder block style options labeled `Glass`; preserve existing saved values by rendering old `glass` values as a solid “Frosted/Solid” equivalent instead of breaking layouts.
>   - Audit dark contrast for headers, tabs, inputs, placeholders, inactive buttons, selected states, empty states, context menus, floating layers, and page controls.
>
> - **Performance and Bloat**
>   - Follow the React best-practices skill findings:
>     - Avoid barrel imports for Vibe-specific icons; import Radix icons directly from the package exports already in use.
>     - Reduce hot-path `JSON.stringify`: replace publish-state equality with a lightweight layout revision/signature helper or cached comparison that only updates when layout/published layout changes.
>     - Add `content-visibility: auto` and stable intrinsic sizing to canvas block wrappers and long palette/layer lists.
>     - Memoize tab panels, palette category sections, layer rows, inspector groups, and canvas blocks where prop identity is stable.
>     - Use `useDeferredValue` for palette/command search input filtering if typing currently recomputes large lists immediately.
>   - Keep lazy route loading intact; do not remove backend features or hidden Construct routes in this pass.
>   - Remove Vibe-facing glass/shadow-heavy hover effects that trigger extra paint; prefer border/color/opacity transitions.
>
> ## Test Plan
> - Run:
>   - `npx -p node@24 npm run lint`
>   - `npx -p node@24 npm run build`
>   - `npx -p node@24 npm test -- --run`
> - Browser QA:
>   - Open workspace and editor.
>   - Confirm new serif V logo appears in auth/sidebar/editor and no old gradient block logo remains on Vibe surfaces.
>   - Use each left tab: Insert, Edit, Page, Site.
>   - Add blocks from palette, select/click away/reselect, edit content/style/advanced fields, duplicate, move, delete, undo/redo.
>   - Open detached Layers panel, select blocks, reorder/move, hide/show, duplicate, delete, close/reopen.
>   - Create/rename/delete pages and navigate between pages.
>   - Save/publish, then verify public route renders without editor chrome and without draft leakage.
>   - Check desktop/tablet/mobile preview controls and zoom.
> - Visual QA:
>   - Confirm no visible glassmorphism/backdrop blur remains in builder/workspace/auth surfaces touched.
>   - Check contrast for labels, inactive tabs, disabled buttons, placeholder text, selection rings, toasts, and floating menus.
>   - Confirm builder chrome is visibly denser while published site content remains unchanged.
> - Performance QA:
>   - Build a 40+ block page.
>   - Verify drag/reorder, tab switching, inspector typing, search, autosave, and publish remain responsive.
>   - Compare production build output for reduced or unchanged bundle size; investigate if the main chunk grows.
>
> ## Assumptions
> - “30% smaller” applies to builder chrome, not generated website content.
> - Use Radix icons only for this pass; no new icon dependency.
> - No functional behavior should be removed, including demo fallback, SELISE persistence, media upload, command palette, context menu, responsive preview, and public renderer.
> - Existing saved `glass` block values must continue rendering gracefully as solid/opacity-based styles.
</details>

> Browser QA caught an important contrast bug: this app redefines Tailwind `white`, so `text-white` is actually rendering dark in the dark theme. I’m patching the visible Vibe gradient/showcase surfaces to use explicit off-white values instead of the overridden token.

> The visual browser pass is good: workspace contrast is fixed, the editor tabs switch cleanly, the inspector lives in the left rail, and the navigator floats/ closes correctly. Implemented the polish pass.

The builder now has the serif V mark, Vibe-facing chrome uses Radix icons, the editor is a compact left-tab studio rail (`Insert`, `Edit`, `Page`, `Site`), and Layers/Navigator is a detached floating panel. I also removed visible blur/glass treatments from the Vibe surfaces touched here, fixed the nasty `text-white` contrast bug caused by the theme override, made primary buttons readable again, and added a few performance touches like deferred palette search, memoized palette rows, `content-visibility`, and cheaper publish-state comparison.

Verified:
- `npx -p node@24 npm run lint` passes with the same 3 existing warnings.
- `npx -p node@24 npm run build` passes.
- `npm test -- --run` passed once; after the final contrast tweak, a full rerun hit a timeout in unrelated legacy `chat-users`, and that file passed when rerun alone.
- Browser QA checked workspace contrast, editor tabs, inspector editing, floating Layers close behavior, and the new button/logo treatment.

One note: the huge legacy app-shell chunk is still there from the Construct starter routes, but the builder chunks themselves stayed leaner after the icon and layout pass.

> `lint` is clean and the production build passes. The one clear engineering warning is bundle size: the old Construct shell still ships a huge legacy chunk, while the Vibe editor itself is moderate but growing. I’ll do one test pass too, then I’ll summarize the actual gaps.

I re-grounded on the repo, Cursor transcript, SELISE notes, and current browser state. No code changes from me in this pass.

Good news first: the app is much farther along now. `lint`, `build`, and the full Vitest suite pass under Node 24. Browser state shows the workspace is dark, readable, and functional. VibeBuilder now has multi-page sites, templates, 50+ block types, nested layout containers, multi-image asset selection, draggable Layers, DragOverlay, adjustable studio width, publish/draft separation, and Blocks Data Gateway/Storage paths.

**What’s Missing**
1. **True editor QA is still under-tested**
   The test suite passes, but there are basically no Vibe-specific interaction tests. The builder’s riskiest flows are still verified mostly by manual browser use: drag/drop, nested containers, asset picker, publish, page creation, inspector editing.

2. **Image persistence needs a hard SELISE check**
   Uploads use `getPreSignedUrlForUpload`, then store `response.uploadUrl.split('?')[0]` as the asset URL in [vibe-builder.service.ts](./src/modules/vibe-builder/services/vibe-builder.service.ts). That may work, but presigned upload URLs are not always the correct durable public/read URL. This needs real upload -> refresh -> publish -> public route verification.

3. **Blocks schemas/RLS need portal verification**
   The frontend assumes `VibeWebsites`, `VibePages`, and `VibeAssets` exist with generated GraphQL operations and owner isolation. Code is aligned with SELISE Data Gateway patterns, but the actual Blocks Cloud schema/RLS rules must be verified in the portal/Data Playground.

4. **Elementor-level layout is still partial**
   There are `section`, `container`, and `stack` nested blocks, but not a full section/column/container model with visual child drop zones, column resizing, gap controls per breakpoint, and empty-container affordances. The `columns` block is still content-list based, not a true nested layout grid.

5. **Performance needs one final tightening pass**
   The Vibe editor chunk is reasonable, but the legacy Construct app still ships a massive `index` chunk around 3.87 MB minified / 1.1 MB gzip. Also `layoutsDeepEqual` still does whole-layout `JSON.stringify` for publish-state comparison, which can become expensive on large pages.

6. **Published-site forms are visual, not wired**
   Contact/newsletter blocks render, but I don’t see real submission handling through SELISE Workflow/Communication/Data Gateway. If the brief expects functional forms, that’s a gap.

**What Needs Work Next**
I’d do one final “stability + proof” pass, not another broad feature burst:

1. Add focused Vibe tests for store/tree operations, AssetPicker multi-select, page create/delete, and published renderer draft-vs-live behavior.
2. Verify real SELISE upload URLs and fix asset URL handling if Blocks returns a better download/public URL.
3. Use Blocks Cloud/Data Playground to confirm schemas, generated operation names, RLS, and owner isolation.
4. Improve nested layout UX: empty container drop zones, clearer insertion indicators, column/container controls, and responsive spacing controls.
5. Add real form submission using Blocks Data Gateway or Workflow/Communication.
6. Reduce bundle risk: lazy-load heavy legacy modules where possible and replace layout equality with a revision/signature approach.
7. Browser QA every template: create, edit, upload image, add page, publish, open public route, test mobile/tablet/desktop.

Bottom line: VibeBuilder is now a strong class-project MVP and visually much more credible. The remaining work is mostly “make it trustworthy”: real SELISE verification, Vibe-specific tests, image durability, nested layout polish, and form submission behavior.

Implemented the visual asset pass.

I used the built-in `image_gen` skill to generate two project-bound raster assets, then converted them to lightweight WebP for runtime use:

- [workspace-hero.webp](./public/vibe-assets/workspace-hero.webp)
- [auth-showcase.webp](./public/vibe-assets/auth-showcase.webp)

I also added a sharper geometric V identity and supporting SVG assets:

- [vibe-mark.svg](./public/vibe-assets/vibe-mark.svg)
- [favicon.svg](./public/favicon.svg)
- [og-card.svg](./public/og-card.svg)
- Template preview assets in [public/vibe-assets](./public/vibe-assets)

Wired them into:

- Workspace hero and site cards in [workspace-dashboard.tsx](./src/modules/vibe-builder/pages/workspace-dashboard.tsx)
- Auth/login showcase in [auth-layout.tsx](./src/layout/auth-layout/auth-layout.tsx)
- Vibe logo component in [vibe-brand.tsx](./src/components/core/vibe-brand/vibe-brand.tsx)
- App metadata/preloads in [index.html](./index.html)

Verification: `npx -p node@24 npm run lint` passes, `npx -p node@24 npm run build` passes, and I visually checked the workspace in Chrome. The new imagery reads well with the dark UI, keeps contrast intact, and the runtime WebP assets are small: about 48 KB and 64 KB.

I continued the pass and fixed a few concrete things.

I added a stronger Vibe registry/inspector regression at [component-registry.spec.tsx](./src/modules/vibe-builder/components/component-registry.spec.tsx). It now covers all 57 registered blocks, renders every block, opens Content/Style/Advanced for each one, and exercises every exposed field control, including nested list-item controls. So yes: the options/tabs are now tested systematically in code, not just by vibes and clicking.

I also cleaned up:
- [command.tsx](./src/components/ui-kit/command.tsx): removed duplicated `displayName` assignments and replaced the lingering Lucide search icon with Radix.
- [command-palette.tsx](./src/modules/vibe-builder/components/command-palette.tsx): added an accessible search label.
- [properties-inspector.tsx](./src/modules/vibe-builder/components/properties-inspector.tsx): added test hooks for icon/list controls so they’re covered reliably.
- [vibe-builder.service.ts](./src/modules/vibe-builder/services/vibe-builder.service.ts): removed the remaining Vibe fallback console warning and kept demo image uploads persistent as data URLs.

Verification:
- `npx -p node@24 npm run lint` passed.
- `npx -p node@24 npm run build` passed.
- Full test suite passed: `66 passed | 1 skipped`, `668 passed | 2 skipped | 1 todo`.
- Final targeted Vibe suite passed: `116 passed`.
- Browser-verified editor tabs, command palette, inspector Content/Style/Advanced after reselect, public published route, metadata after render settle, no editor chrome on public route, and no browser console warnings/errors.

- Add a real Playwright/Cypress e2e suite for drag geometry, deletion flows, uploads, and publish flows.
- Add SELISE contract tests for real Data Gateway/Storage schemas so local demo fallback and production backend can’t silently drift.

- Hero `Right` alignment was behaving like left alignment. Fixed.
- Columns exposed alignment controls, but the renderer ignored them. Fixed.

Changed [block-thumbnail.tsx](./src/modules/vibe-builder/components/block-thumbnail.tsx): removed the traffic-light buttons, removed the wavy ornament, toned down the frame, and adjusted previews to show the real structure of each block more clearly. > That error path makes sense: the server-side logout is trying to refresh/recover a token, then SELISE rejects localhost with `Invalid_Origin_Or_Referer`. For logout, that’s the wrong user experience anyway: even if remote logout fails, the app should clear the local session and get you out immediately. I’ll patch logout to be local-first/fail-safe.
>

> I found the bug: `signout()` deletes persisted auth before calling the Blocks logout endpoint, then `clients.post` sees the 401 and enters the automatic refresh path. That refresh request is what fails with `Invalid_Origin_Or_Referer`, so the UI shows an error even though you wanted to leave. I’m changing logout to never refresh and to clear local auth regardless of remote logout success.

Fixed. Logout is now fail-safe.

What was happening: the app called SELISE `/Logout`, got a `401`, then the HTTP client tried to refresh the session. SELISE rejected that refresh from localhost with `Invalid_Origin_Or_Referer`, so logout surfaced as “Something went wrong.”

I changed [auth.service.ts](./src/modules/auth/services/auth.service.ts) so logout:
- uses `postWithoutSessionRefresh`, so it never enters token refresh
- treats remote SELISE logout as best-effort
- always clears local auth and returns success
- sends you back to `/login`

Implemented the rebrand to **Blockloom**.

I chose it after checking that stronger “obvious” names like [Sitewright](https://sitewright.co/), [PageWright](https://www.pagewright.net/), [PageCraft](https://pagecraft.me/), and [SiteForge](https://siteforge.io/) are already close to active web products. Blockloom has some unrelated existing uses, so treat this as a product/class-project name, not a formal trademark clearance.

Changed the visible product identity across:
- [brand component](./src/components/core/vibe-brand/vibe-brand.tsx)
- [index metadata/title](./index.html)
- [favicon/PWA/OG assets](./public/favicon.svg)
- auth/login/signup copy, workspace hero, onboarding, public-site footer, demo org/email labels, templates, and invoice branding.

I kept internal `Vibe*` Data Gateway schema/type names intact where changing them could break SELISE persistence.

Verification passed:
- `npx -p node@24 npm run lint`
- `npx -p node@24 npm run build`
- `npx -p node@24 npm test -- --run` → 682 passed, existing skipped/todo unchanged
- Chrome visual check on `http://127.0.0.1:3000/login`: title, install prompt, wordmark, login heading, and favicon now show Blockloom.

Your SELISE deployed tab will still show old branding until you deploy the updated build.
